proxies_declared.valid_for_the_claim: only as validated: PC3 replays it against the recorded w_total at every gate call and the exact-match fraction is reported per arm per seed

proxies_declared.valid_for_the_claim: YES in a LIVE cell; a DRY cell's W is submit-to-SETTLE and must never be compared against it

proxies_declared.actually_measures: delivered after the deadline under the committed D144/D146 delivery rewrites
proxies_declared.valid_for_the_claim: YES for the pre-registered harm bound, which is stated on robot LATE

variance_caveat: LIVE-TRAJECTORY VARIANCE BETWEEN r1 AND r2 AT THE SAME SEED IS NOT MEASURED. These are live cells against a real engine, so the same seed fixes the workload and the arrival trace but NOT the server's own timing, and a same-seed difference is therefore not automatically causal. To bound it would need repeat cells of ONE unchanged arm at one seed, which do not exist for -r1 or -r2; the nearest bound available is the committed covex-v6-state-shares_n16_s5 rerun pattern used elsewhere in this tree, which is a different arm. Until such repeats exist, a same-seed delta smaller than the unmeasured replicate spread cannot be attributed to the register change, and the s4 regression is reported as what the cells say rather than as an established causal effect.

consistency_check_1_cross_check_against_.method: every quantity here that has been measured before is cross-checked against its committed value. The committed sources are the cells' own cell.json (PC1, exact on all six cells), the r1 residual diagnosis `d187_r1_residual_diagnosis.json` for the r1 size/queue split, and `reports/prereg_queue_register_r2.md` for the retention denominators.

retention_reconciliation.definition: check 2 retention = (shares_on_time - base_on_time) / (rung2_uo_on_time - base_on_time), the D177 quantity, NOT `by_deadline`, which is an accuracy that re-admits the device answer and runs in the flattering direction.
retention_reconciliation.denominators_taken_from: reports/prereg_queue_register_r2.md and the StudyD179-SHARES row: s4 base 35/132, committed rung 2 (uo) 118/132. NOT recomputed here, and declared as a quoted input rather than a measurement of this run.

positive_control_on_the_definition.why_this_matters: the definition is validated against a COMMITTED value before it is applied to r2, so the r2 figure is not the first use of an unchecked formula

retention_reconciliation.r2_s4_vs_the_0_90_bar: FAILS, and is WORSE than r1's 0.7229
retention_reconciliation.s6: r1 and r2 are both 92 on-time, so check 2 retention is IDENTICAL at s6 and the 0.77 figure is unchanged. The target seed did not move at all.

consistency_check_1_cross_check_against_.check_3_distribution_sanity: every median in this file is reported with min, p25, p75, max, mean and IQR, and the per-skip values are kept in full under q1 and recall_skip_rows, because the populations are 9 to 47 items and a median alone would hide the composition change that is the answer to question 4. No constant appears where a distribution is expected; the one exact-equality worth flagging is release_infeasible TOTAL at s4, 2,375 under both arms, which is a coincidence of a falling alert count against a rising recall and assistance count (2,341+34 against 2,322+6+47) and not a shared constant: the per-type counts all differ and the per-event lists are not equal.
consistency_check_1_cross_check_against_.check_6_proxy_validity: see proxies_declared; the primary q2 measure uses none
consistency_check_1_cross_check_against_.check_7_validate_the_control: the CONTROL side of this comparison is r1, and it is audited on its own numbers before the comparison is read: PC1 reproduces its committed robot_pool_on_time and robot_pool_n on all three seeds, its size/queue split reproduces the committed r1 diagnosis exactly at s4 AND s5, and its retention formula reproduces the committed 0.7229. A POSITIVE CONTROL is included in the same move: the committed r1 s4 split 9/25 is a known-good value and this reader returns it exactly, so the classifier is not broken.

pc1_committed_headline.path_note: the committed headline lives at cell.json score.score.sweep[0]; `score.sweep` is NOT the path and reads None, which is recorded here so the wrong path cannot be read as a zero

pc3_w_reconstruction.gates_only_the_secondary_measure: This control gates ONLY the per-reason W RECONSTRUCTION. It does NOT gate q1, q3, q4, q5 or the primary q2 measure, all of which read direct fields. Where it fails, the reconstruction is reported as SECONDARY and no headline rests on it.
pc3_w_reconstruction.known_residual: The replay understates the logged w_total by a median of one alert charge. The charge AMOUNTS are right (the engine-uncached variant scores far worse), so the residual is the DRAIN INSTANT: the tracker is popped from the coordinator's epoch loop when it processes the first-token hook, which is strictly later than the engine's logged t_first_token, and no log carries that instant. Settling instead of first-token over-drains in the other direction (0.386 exact, median +380). The truth lies between two conventions neither of which is logged, which is why the primary q2 measure does not use this reconstruction at all.

q2_oversize_share_of_W.method: PRIMARY measure is DIRECT: the oversize-in-flight detector of `oversize_intervals`, whose start, size and type are logged fields and whose end is read off the logged `w_by_type` series. The denominator is the DIRECT fed queue value at the skip. The per-reason W reconstruction is reported beside it as a SECONDARY cross-read and is NOT used for any headline, because its PC3 exact-match rate is below the bar.

verdict.headline: r2 is a REFUTED MECHANISM under its own pre-registered failure condition. The queue-refused recall skips did not fall: 25 -> 32 at s4 and 7 -> 9 at s6, the two TARGET seeds. The prereg says in terms: 'if the queue-refused skips do not fall, the named mechanism is wrong and is reported as wrong. The fix is not kept for being harmless.'
verdict.rule_2_classification: FIRED AND DID NOT HELP. This is NOT an absent link and NOT inconclusive: the switch reached decisions (release_infeasible_alert fell at all three seeds, 2341->2322, 2678->2195, 2022->1738; the fed queue value at the s4 recall skips fell from a median of 1,481 to 1,101) and the mechanism operated as specified. It produced no gain on the robot pool and a material loss at s4. Under Rule 2 that is the one category that is evidence about the policy.
verdict.but_it_is_still_not_a_settled_negative_b: Rule 2 requires a Step 4 control showing the control changes the result, and live-trajectory variance between r1 and r2 at the same seed is NOT MEASURED here. See variance_caveat. The refutation stands against the PRE-REGISTERED BAR, which is what the prereg asked, and that is a weaker claim than a measured causal effect.

two_claims_that_must_not_be_merged.the_register_fix_is_CORRECT_ON_ITS_OWN_T: YES, and nothing here disturbs it. The D162 regressor is built over the interval t_submit to t_submit + first_token_s (cost_model_gate_d162.py:97), so submit-to-FIRST-TOKEN work is the quantity its coefficient was fitted on, and `self._w.total()` is that quantity while `_uncached_in_flight` is not. Feeding a model the quantity it was fitted on is right independently of what the policy then does. This diagnosis does not weaken that.
two_claims_that_must_not_be_merged.it_is_REFUTED_AS_A_LEVER_FOR_CHECK_2: YES. Check 2 retention is unchanged at s6 (92 on-time under both arms) and falls at s4 from 0.7229 to 0.5301. The 25 queue-refused skips the prereg identified as the reachable population were not converted into on-time answers; 32 queue-refused skips appear instead.
two_claims_that_must_not_be_merged.these_are_different_claims: A correct input and a useful lever are not the same proposition. The first is about the model; the second is about the policy. Reporting them together as one verdict is the register error this project keeps hitting in the other direction.
two_claims_that_must_not_be_merged.recommendation: NOT RECOMMENDED on correctness grounds alone, BECAUSE IT MADE s4 WORSE: robot on time 95 -> 79, release_infeasible_recall 34 -> 47, share_deny_recall 467 -> 643, retention 0.7229 -> 0.5301. Keeping a correct input that costs 16 robot answers at the primary seed is a trade-off, not a cleanup. THAT IS THE USER'S CALL and is not decided here. r1 IS THE BEST SHARES VERSION on the evidence in these cells.

verdict.the_mechanism_of_the_regression_in_one_c: r2 feeds a SMALLER queue term, so the re-check admits MORE work earlier. Three consequences, each measured: (a) recall-type gate calls rise 2,442 -> 3,246 at s4 and admits 1,975 -> 2,603, so w[recall] is non-zero more often and the D179 (3) oversize SERIALISATION rule denies more: oversize_wait_for_own_type 444 -> 615, which is 171 of the 176 rise in share_deny_recall. (b) W rises run-wide, not falls: the logged w_total median goes 1,816 -> 1,900 and p75 2,618 -> 2,858, and W sits at or above the ALERT floor 6,357 -> 7,428 times, so alert share denials rise 1,891 -> 2,367. (c) background build pieces are squeezed, so the subtracted prefix at a later recall is SHALLOWER by exactly one 1,024-token piece on 10 of the 31 shared skips, which raises u and converts queue-refusals into SIZE-refusals: 9 -> 15. The two mechanisms are COUPLED THROUGH W and r2 MOVED THE BOTTLENECK rather than removing it, which is exactly the hypothesis question 3 proposed.
verdict.the_users_question_2_answered: NO, oversize work is NOT what makes W large at the moments that matter, and it is NOT the explanation for the r2 regression. The mechanism is real and large WHERE IT FIRES: across every logged gate call an oversize-admitted request is in W at 17.0 percent of instants under r1 and 17.3 percent under r2, and where present it is a median 58.7 / 58.2 percent of the logged w_total. But it is UNCHANGED between the two arms, and at the s4 recall skips it got RARER, not commoner: 7 of 34 skips under r1 against 5 of 47 under r2, median share of the fed W exactly 0.0 under both. Oversize admissions themselves fell 328 -> 320 and their total seconds in W are 268.9 against 269.9, a 0.4 percent difference. A quantity that does not change between the compared branches cannot carry the difference. The one place the hypothesis does describe the data is the s6 PEAK stratum, reported with its size: the 4 largest-fed-W r2 skips (13,048 to 15,354) ALL have an oversize request in flight at 65 to 100 percent of W, and r1's single largest (14,094) does too, so the peak mechanism exists at both and still does not separate them.
verdict.what_would_be_needed_to_bound_the_varian: repeat cells of ONE UNCHANGED arm at ONE seed, at least three, scored the same way, to give a replicate spread for robot_pool_on_time and for release_infeasible_recall. No such repeats exist for -r1 or -r2. Until they do, the s4 delta of 16 robot answers is reported as what these cells say and not as a measured causal effect of the register change. The direction is nevertheless consistent across three independent mechanisms measured on counters that are far outside any plausible replicate noise (oversize_wait_for_own_type +171, share_at_or_above_floor_alert +1,071, share_deny_alert +476), which is why the coupling account is reported as the mechanism while the headline magnitude is not.
